 1   justly proud to honor Edith M. Flanigen upon the

 3   National Medal of Technology and Innovation; this 

 4   auspicious occasion was recognized by President 

 5   Obama with a ceremony at the White House on 

 6   Thursday, November 20, 2014; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, The National Medal of 

 8   Technology and Innovation is the nation's  

 9   highest honor for technological achievement, 

10   bestowed by the President of the United States on  

11   America's leading innovators; the medal is 

12   awarded annually to individuals for their  

13   outstanding contributions to America's economic,  

14   environmental and social well-being; and 

15                "WHEREAS, Born January 28, 1929, in 

16   Buffalo, New York, Edith M. Flanigen's early 

17   interest in chemistry was sparked by a teacher 

18   she had while attending Holy Angels Academy with 

19   her two sisters; and 

20                "WHEREAS, Edith M. Flanigen studied 

21   chemistry at D'Youville College, where she 

22   graduated as class president and valedictorian; 

23   she went on to earn a master's degree in 

24   inorganic physical chemistry from Syracuse 

25   University in 1952; and 


                                                                3400

 1                "WHEREAS, A true trailblazer in her 

 2   field, Edith M. Flanigen began her illustrious 

 3   career at Union Carbide in 1952, first tasked 

 4   with the purification/extraction of different 

 5   silicone polymers; she quickly moved up the 

 6   ladder to the Molecular Sieves Group, followed by  

 7   her promotion as the first female Corporate 

 8   Research Fellow, and finally as Senior Corporate 

 9   Research Fellow in 1986; and 

10                "WHEREAS, In 1988, Edith M. Flanigen 

11   moved to Universal Oil Products (UOP), now known 

12   as Honeywell, where she was once again named 

13   Senior Research Fellow; just three years later 

14   she was promoted to UOP Fellow; she retired from 

15   this esteemed position in 1994, but remained 

16   active with the company as a consultant until 

17   2004; and 

18                "WHEREAS, During her 42-year tenure 

19   as a chemist, Edith M. Flanigen was instrumental 

20   in the development of a way to manufacture more 

21   gasoline from every barrel of oil, as well as a 

22   way to extract organics out of paint; she was 

23   cited by President Obama for her role in helping 

24   decontaminate radioactive water at the Fukushima 

25   Daiichi nuclear power plant in Japan; and

18   85, is retired and living in White Plains, 

19   New York; she is an active member at the Church
